rows.comment: Compact status with a time placeholder.
lineComments: Says what comes next and for how long.

rows.comment: Compact status with a time placeholder.
lineComments: Says what comes next and for how long.

rows.comment: Explains the state but gives no recovery step, and 'nothing is arriving' is vague.
lineComments: Name the missing data (heart rate) and tell the reader to reconnect.
rows.replacement: The band is not connected. Reconnect it to record heart rate for this session.

rows.comment: The 'so it needs to be' chain is awkward. Split into a fact and an instruction.
lineComments: Fact first, then the fit instruction, which is worth keeping.
rows.replacement: The band is connected but has sent no heartbeat yet. Wear it snug, a finger-width above the wrist bone.

rows.comment: 'Fix' is undefined jargon and the passive 'when asked' hides the actor.
lineComments: Name the app as the requester and say 'location' instead of 'fix'.
rows.replacement: The phone returned an error when the app requested its location.

lineComments: Say the app receives no location rather than 'no fixes are arriving'.
rows.replacement: Location services are off on this phone, so the app receives no location.

lineComments: Carries pool length and stroke, nothing else.

rows.comment: Sanskrit proper noun used as the pose name.
'Start pinned' and 'fixes settle' are shorthand and the semicolon packs two ideas.
lineComments: Split into two plain sentences; say location points instead of fixes.
rows.replacement: Start point marked. Distance shows once enough location points are recorded.

lineComments: Use 'location points' for the same thing.
rows.replacement: {distance} from the location points recorded so far.

rows.comment: Compact subtitle with placeholders and plural.
lineComments: Weight and set count, nothing extra.
Tells the reader what to do.

rows.comment: 'Rather than fired hours after you meant it' rebuts a case nobody raised, and the sentences are dense. The behaviour (old-timestamp taps are dropped) is worth keeping.
lineComments: Condition, mechanism, outcome in three short sentences, no contrast clause.
rows.replacement: Taps work only while the app is connected and awake. If you tap while your phone is away, the band stores the tap and sends it later with an old timestamp. The app ignores it.

rows.comment: Question matches what a reader would ask when the actions are missing.
Wordy, uses a semicolon, and 'either way' is filler. The recovery step should be its own sentence.
lineComments: Cause, recovery step, and what still works, as three sentences.
rows.replacement: Ring phone and flashlight are hidden because the app could not check which actions this device allows. Reopen the app and return to this screen. The in-app actions above still work.

rows.comment: Em dash, and the ambiguous 'it' appears twice.
lineComments: Say the save failed and what to expect, without a dash.
rows.replacement: Saving failed. The change may be lost when you reopen the app.

rows.comment: States what iOS does, useful to the reader.
Accessibility suffix appended to a label.
States the effect of the setting; privacy-relevant so left as is.
lineComments: Direct statement of state and effect.

rows.comment: Uses a curly apostrophe, and 'once it is final' leaves 'it' unclear.
lineComments: Straight apostrophe; name the day as the thing that must be final.
rows.replacement: Writes each day's sleep, resting heart rate, HRV, respiratory rate, energy and workouts to {store} once that day is final

rows.comment: States the problem and the action.
States the problem and the action.
States the problem and the action.
The privacy statement stays, but the punchy fragment 'Nothing will be.' is flourish. Meaning is unchanged.
lineComments: One sentence with the same two commitments.
rows.replacement: Nothing has been uploaded, and nothing will be.

rows.comment: Keeps every privacy fact (one copy, date, latest copy only, withdrawal message sent once, not retried, deletion not confirmable). Removes the em dash and the passive 'we tried to tell it'.
lineComments: First line states the current effect; keep as is.
Split the long final line into short sentences naming the app as actor.
rows.replacement:
Nothing further will be uploaded.

One copy of your database was uploaded on {date}. The server keeps only the most recent copy per device. The app sent a one-time message withdrawing your consent. It is not retried, so if this phone was offline the message did not arrive, and the app cannot confirm the copy is deleted.

rows.comment: Consent prompt title, a direct question.
Consent copy must stay strong, and it does. Fixes: the em dash, passive 'is used', and the hedged 'not anonymous in any meaningful sense', which becomes a flat statement.
lineComments: Upload schedule and scope are exact; keep them, swap the dash for a colon and name the purpose in its own sentence.
State plainly that the copy is not anonymous and what it contains; keep the opt-out.
rows.replacement:
Once a day, on Wi-Fi and while charging, a compressed copy of your ENTIRE database is uploaded: every derived day and every raw sensor row the band has sent. The upload is used to improve the algorithms.

The copy is not anonymous. It contains your whole health history. You can switch this off at any time, and nothing further is sent from that moment.
